2027-05-24.title: Monday of the Eighth Week in Ordinary Time
readings: Turn back to the Lord and forsake your sins (Lectionary numbering: Sirach 17:20–24)
Let the just exult and rejoice in the Lord
Go, sell what you own, and give the money to the poor; then come, follow me
2027-05-24.alt: Weekday of Ordinary Time, Week 8 (Year I). Liturgical colour: green. The Lectionary cites the first reading as Sirach 17:20–24; in the NRSV and in the Malayalam POC Bible the same verses are numbered 17:24–29. Today Salesian communities and many parishes in India honour Mary, Help of Christians; Pope Benedict XVI asked that 24 May also be a World Day of Prayer for the Church in China, under the protection of Our Lady of Sheshan.
2027-05-24.verse: Jesus looked at them and said, “For mortals it is impossible, but not for God; for God all things are possible.”
theo: Ben Sira today speaks to anyone who has wandered away from God, and his tone is full of hope. “Yet to those who repent he grants a return, and he encourages those who are losing hope.” God does not merely allow a return; he grants it, opens the road, and even comes to meet those whose courage is failing. Then the invitation, in three urgent verbs: “Turn back to the Lord and forsake your sins; pray in his presence and lessen your offense. Return to the Most High and turn away from iniquity.” Ben Sira, who wrote before the full revelation of the resurrection, adds a reason drawn from life itself: the living give thanks, the dead are silent, so “those who are alive and well sing the Lord's praises.” Today, while we have breath, is the time to return. And he ends with a cry of wonder: “How great is the mercy of the Lord, and his forgiveness for those who return to him!” The Psalm gives the experience of one who has made that return: “While I kept silence, my body wasted away … Then I acknowledged my sin to you … and you forgave the guilt of my sin.” Hiding sin makes us sick; confessing it heals. “Happy are those whose transgression is forgiven.”

The Gospel tells of a man who runs up to Jesus and kneels before him: “Good Teacher, what must I do to inherit eternal life?” He is sincere, eager, respectful. Jesus points him first to God, “No one is good but God alone,” and then to the commandments, especially those about the neighbour. “Teacher, I have kept all these since my youth.” And then comes one of the most tender lines in the Gospels: “Jesus, looking at him, loved him.” Out of that love comes the invitation: “You lack one thing; go, sell what you own, and give the money to the poor, and you will have treasure in heaven; then come, follow me.” The man “was shocked and went away grieving, for he had many possessions.” He did not lose the love of Jesus; he lost the courage to accept it. Jesus then turns to the disciples: “How hard it will be for those who have wealth to enter the kingdom of God! … It is easier for a camel to go through the eye of a needle.” The disciples are astounded: “Then who can be saved?” And Jesus answers with the sentence that is the hope of every one of us: “For mortals it is impossible, but not for God; for God all things are possible.” Not everyone is called to sell everything, but every disciple is called to hold nothing more tightly than Christ. The rich man went away; Ben Sira tells us the door of return is always open. Today, as many honour Mary, Help of Christians, we ask her to help us let go of whatever keeps us from following her Son, and we pray, as the Church asks, for the Catholics of China.
outline: Ask: what is the one thing I would find hardest to give up for Jesus?
God opens the road home and encourages those losing hope.
Point 2 · Looking at him, loved him
The love of Jesus comes before the challenge.
Point 3 · For God all things are possible
What is impossible for us, grace makes possible.
live: Make a quiet examination of conscience tonight, and plan to receive the sacrament of Reconciliation this week.
Give away one possession you are attached to, or give a generous gift to the poor this week, as an act of trust in Jesus.
2027-05-24.prayer: Merciful Father, how great is your mercy and your forgiveness for those who return to you. Open for us the road home, and encourage us when we are losing hope. Lord Jesus, you looked at the rich man and loved him; look at us with the same love, and give us the courage to let go of whatever we hold more tightly than you. Mary, Help of Christians, help us to follow your Son; and protect the Church in China and all who suffer for their faith. For you, O God, all things are possible. Amen.
altar: The Lord who “looked at him and loved him” looks at us from the altar. He who had no possessions on the cross gives us the only treasure that lasts, himself, in his Body and Blood. To receive him is to receive the grace that makes the impossible possible: a heart that can let go and follow.

quick: Ben Sira: God grants a return to those who repent; turn back to the Lord; how great is his mercy.
A rich man asks Jesus about eternal life; Jesus, looking at him, loves him and invites him to sell all, give to the poor and follow.
The man goes away grieving; Jesus says: for mortals it is impossible, but not for God; for God all things are possible.
2027-05-24.action: Give away one thing you are attached to, or make a generous gift to the poor this week.
2027-05-24.question: What do I hold more tightly than I hold Jesus?

family.explain: A man who had lots of money and things came running to Jesus. Jesus looked at him with love and said: give your things to the poor, and come with me. But the man went away sad, because he loved his things too much. Jesus loves us too, and he wants our hearts to love him more than any toy or phone or money.
family.intention: We pray for poor families who have very little, for the Church in China, and, through Mary Help of Christians, for all who are in trouble.
family.ask: Ask: “Is there something in our house we could give to someone who needs it more than we do?”

illus: A young software engineer in Bengaluru, with a good salary and a new car, began volunteering on Sundays at a home for abandoned elderly people run by sisters. After a year he sold the car, bought a scooter, and used the difference to pay for medicines at the home. His friends thought he had gone mad. He said: I am not a hero. Jesus did not ask me to sell everything. He only asked me to stop holding the car more tightly than I hold him. Now I sleep better.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, look at us with love, and give us hearts that let go and follow you. Amen.
share: To those who repent he grants a return (Sirach 17:24). Where do I need to come back to God?
Jesus, looking at him, loved him (Mark 10:21). Can I believe that Jesus looks at me with love, even before I change?
For God all things are possible (Mark 10:27). Which impossible situation in my life do I need to hand over to God?
pm.resp: Let the just exult and rejoice in the Lord.
interc: For all who have drifted away from God, that they may find the road of return open.
For the rich and powerful, that they may use their wealth for the poor.
For the Catholics of China, that they may live their faith in peace and in communion with the whole Church.
Through Mary, Help of Christians, for young people, especially those helped by the Salesian family.
For our group, that we may hold nothing more tightly than Christ.
pm.close: Father, for you all things are possible. Take our hearts and make them wholly yours, through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear friends, Ben Sira gives us good news today. Yet to those who repent he grants a return, and he encourages those who are losing hope (Sirach 17:24). However far we have wandered, the road back to God is not closed. He does not wait with folded arms; he comes to meet those who are losing courage.

The Psalm tells us what it feels like to keep sin hidden: while I kept silence, my body wasted away. And what happens when we confess: I acknowledged my sin to you, and you forgave the guilt of my sin (Psalm 32:3, 5). The sacrament of Reconciliation is the place where this happens for us.

In the Gospel a good man runs to Jesus and kneels. He has kept the commandments since his youth. And Mark says: Jesus, looking at him, loved him (Mark 10:21). Before any challenge, there is love. Then Jesus asks for the one thing he lacked: sell what you own, give to the poor, and come, follow me. The man went away grieving, for he had many possessions. His things owned him.

Most of us are not asked to sell everything. But all of us are asked: is there anything I hold more tightly than Jesus? Money, a house, a career, a relationship, my own plans? If we feel it is impossible to let go, Jesus answers: for mortals it is impossible, but not for God; for God all things are possible (Mark 10:27). Today many honour Mary, Help of Christians. Let us ask her help to let go and follow her Son, and let us pray for our brothers and sisters in China. Amen.
kids: Children, a rich man asked Jesus how to go to heaven. Jesus looked at him with love and said: share your things with the poor and come with me. But the man went away sad, because he loved his things too much. Jesus wants us to love him more than toys, games or phones. Can you share something with someone today?

intro: Theme: “For God all things are possible.”
The road of return that God opens, the loving gaze of Jesus, and the grace that makes the impossible possible.

concl: God always opens the road of return, and his mercy is greater than our sins.
Jesus looks at us with love and asks us to hold nothing more tightly than him; what is impossible for us is possible for God.
2027-05-24.resolve: Make one generous act of letting go this week, and ask Mary, Help of Christians, to help you follow her Son.
